title: A 24% estimate of rain-response loss remained uncertain in 159 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We test whether the lower annual rain response after 1997 remains in adjacent-year changes, which remove a linear additive runoff drift. We use annual CAMELS-AUS v2.03 tables from a prior SCI study. The primary comparison uses 159 matched catchments and 2010-2021 versus 1951-1996. With AGCD rain, the partial current-rain response fell by 23.8%; SILO gave 21.8%. Differencing did not remove the point loss. But a joint bootstrap of synchronous three-year blocks and two-degree spatial cells gave 95% intervals of -43.6% to +6.4% and -42.1% to +9.3%. A curved rain relation gave smaller losses and wider intervals. All eight main three-year intervals included zero. An exploratory spatial-only interval was -31.6% to -17.5%, with regional years held fixed. Omitting one recent pair at a time left all point estimates negative. Thus a linear drift does not explain away the estimate, but shared regional year variation limits its precision. These are reused observations, not independent replication. Only 11 recent pair endpoints, uncertain bootstrap coverage, amplified observation error, and unstable curved fits limit inference. No physical cause or onset date is identified. Code, compatible inputs, draws and audits permit an offline repeat.

display.caption: The same adjacent-year estimate has narrow spatial-only uncertainty and wider joint year and space uncertainty. Omitting one pair at a time leaves negative point estimates. These checks are exploratory.
Partial rain-response changes in levels and adjacent-year differences. Bars use joint spatial-cell and synchronous three-year-block resampling. The 2010-2021 intervals all include zero.
